newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares up 2.6 pct on Chidambaram's comments.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares up 2.6 pct on Chidambaram's comments.

text.p: Bombay shares rallied in hectic trade at the start of the new trade setttlement on Monday, after the finance minister said a controversial tax on companies may soon be phased out, dealers said.
"This bit of good news is a tonic for the markets," said Antony Sequeira, managing director at Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) jumped 75.84 points, or 2.63 percent to end at 2,956.99 provisional close, off 2,966.99, the day's high.

"The introduction of MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax) in the last budget has caused a high degree of discomfort to industry," finance minister P. Chidambaram told a recent seminar organised in Bombay by the International Association of Lawyers, newspapers reported on Monday.
"It was introduced as a number of companies were paying dividend but not tax," he said.
Dealers said the finance minister's statement gave a boost to market sentiments with speculators building positions in pivotal stocks.
Chidambaram said the new tax may be phased out after a new Income Tax Act and Companies Act came into force.
The Unit Trust of India, the country's biggest mutual fund was a major buyer in index-linked stocks, helping them stage a sharp rally, traders said.

ACC rose 89.50 rupees to 1,100, TELCO 18.50 to 336.50, Bajaj Auto 31.0 to 771.0, TISCO 5.25 to 158.75, Gujarat Ambuja 6.25 to 239.25, SBI 9.50 to 218.25, Nestle 15.0 to 195.0, Reliance 6.75 to 194.50 and MTNL 6.50 to 227.25. The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 21.08 points to 846.08.
